Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee, September 17-18, 2026

A joint press conference is scheduled after the conclusion of this meeting.

Staff Review of the Economic Situation

The staff forecast that real GDP increased at a moderate pace through the third quarter. Inflation was running at 2.4 percent in August, still somewhat above the Committee's objective. Conditions in the labor market remained tight, with job gains solid.

Discussion of the Economic Outlook and Monetary Policy

Participants discussed the possibility of further adjustments to the target range. In their discussion of economic conditions, several participants noted that inflation was expected to average 2.2 percent in 2027. Most participants agreed that the risks to the outlook were moving into better balance. One participant preferred to keep the target range unchanged for a longer period. The Committee judged that it would not be appropriate to lower the target range until it had gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent. Participants agreed that future determinations of monetary policy would depend on the incoming data. All participants affirmed their strong commitment to returning inflation to the Committee's 2 percent objective.

Staff Review of the Financial Situation

Financial conditions eased somewhat over the intermeeting period, and spreads in credit markets remained narrow.

Committee's Policy Actions

The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4.50 to 4.75 percent. Voting for the policy action: Jerome H. Powell, Chair; … Voting against this action: Christopher J. Waller, who preferred a 25 basis point reduction at this meeting.

Communications

The minutes will be released three weeks after the meeting.
